# Pastry Recipe: Lemon Olive Oil Cake (Pastry Station)

Owner: Lucia Romano (Pastry Cook)

## Overview and Yield
- Style: Moist, fragrant lemon cake using extra-virgin olive oil
- Yield (1x): One 9-inch round cake, 2 inches high, about 12 portions
- Batter: ~5 cups. Works in 9-inch round or 1/4 sheet pan
- Flavor notes: Bright lemon, fruity oil, tender crumb

## Scaled Ingredient Table (Weights prioritized)
| Ingredient | 1x (9-in round) | 2x | 4x |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All-purpose flour | 10 oz (2 cups) | 1 lb 4 oz (4 cups) | 2 lb 8 oz (8 cups) |
| Granulated sugar | 10.5 oz (1 1/2 cups) | 1 lb 5 oz (3 cups) | 2 lb 10 oz (6 cups) |
| Baking powder | 1 3/4 tsp | 3 1/2 tsp | 7 tsp |
| Baking soda | 1/4 tsp | 1/2 tsp | 1 tsp |
| Fine sea salt | 3/4 tsp | 1 1/2 tsp | 1 tbsp |
| Lemon zest (fresh) | 2 tbsp | 1/4 cup | 1/2 cup |
| Large eggs (shelled) | 3 each (~5.25 oz) | 6 each | 12 each |
| Extra-virgin olive oil | 1 cup (8 fl oz) | 2 cups (16 fl oz) | 4 cups (32 fl oz) |
| Whole milk | 3/4 cup (6 fl oz) | 1 1/2 cups (12 fl oz) | 3 cups (24 fl oz) |
| Fresh lemon juice | 1/4 cup (2 fl oz) | 1/2 cup (4 fl oz) | 1 cup (8 fl oz) |
| Vanilla extract | 1 tsp | 2 tsp | 4 tsp |

Notes:
- Zest lemons before juicing. Microplane for fine zest.
- If using volume only, do not pack flour; whisk to aerate before measuring.

## Pan Prep and Tools
- Pans: 9-inch round cake pan (2-inch high) or 1/4 sheet (approx. 9x13 in)
- Line bottom with parchment. Lightly oil and flour sides (use olive oil; no butter if dairy-free)
- Tools: Scale, two mixing bowls, whisk, rubber spatula, Microplane, fine strainer, instant-read thermometer

## Method (1x batch)
1. Heat oven to 350°F. Position rack center. Prep pan as above.
2. Dry mix: In a large bowl whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until uniform.
3. Lemon sugar: Add lemon zest to dry mix. Rub in with fingertips or whisk to disperse oils.
4. Wet mix: In a second bowl whisk eggs until smooth. Stream in olive oil while whisking. Add milk, lemon juice, and vanilla; whisk to combine. Strain if pulpy.
5. Combine: Make a well in dry mix. Add wet mix in two additions. Whisk just until smooth. Do not overmix. Scrape bowl.
6. Rest batter 3–5 minutes to let flour hydrate and bubbles settle.
7. Pan: Pour into prepared pan. Tap lightly to release large bubbles. Smooth top.
8. Bake per table below. Rotate pan at hallway point for even color.
9. Doneness checks (see section). Remove when done; cool in pan 10 minutes, then de-pan to rack. Peel parchment. Cool fully before slicing or wrapping.

## Bake Temps and Times
| Pan | Oven Temp | Bake Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9-inch round, 2 in high | 350°F | 35–42 minutes | Done when center 205°F or toothpick has a few moist crumbs |
| 1/4 sheet (9x13 in) | 350°F | 22–28 minutes | Shallower pan bakes faster; start checking at 20 minutes |

## Doneness Checks
- Internal temp at center: 200–205°F
- Toothpick or cake tester: few moist crumbs, no wet batter
- Top: light golden, small cracks acceptable
- Touch: center springs back; edges just pull from pan

## Portioning and Service
- Standard: 12 wedges from 9-inch round
- For clean cuts: chill 30 minutes, use warm knife, wipe between cuts
- Optional finish: sifted powdered sugar to order; brush warm cake with 2 tbsp lemon juice + 2 tbsp sugar heated to dissolve for extra lemon pop

## Storage and Holding
- Cool to room temp within 2 hours. Do not wrap warm
- Room temp, wrapped: up to 2 days (non-TCS). Keep covered, low humidity, off the line
- Refrigerated, wrapped: up to 5 days. Bring to room temp before service for best texture
- Frozen, double-wrapped: up to 2 months. Thaw wrapped under refrigeration
- Once sliced, cover cut face with parchment or plastic to prevent drying

## Allergen and Dietary Notes
- Contains: eggs, wheat (gluten)
- Dairy present in standard formula (milk)
- Dairy-free option: replace milk 1:1 with unsweetened oat or almond milk + 1 tsp white vinegar per 3/4 cup; grease pan with oil, not butter. Bake times unchanged
- Nut-free formula as written (verify oil brand not processed with nut flavorings)

## Quality and Troubleshooting
- Dense layer at bottom: overmixed or underbaked. Mix just to combine; check oven temp with thermometer
- Greasy crumb: too much oil or under-emulsified. Whisk eggs well before streaming oil
- Bitter pith taste: avoid zesting white pith; use only yellow zest
- Pale top: bake to time and temp; finish last 2–3 minutes without parchment overhang
summary: Pastry station recipe for Lemon Olive Oil Cake with scaled ingredients, method, bake times, doneness checks, storage, and allergen notes.
title: Lemon Olive Oil Cake
